name: Coupa
scope_notes: Covers Coupa (Core platform REST API). Covers customer-created integrations to the Coupa Core platform; Treasury, CSO and Supply Chain products have separate APIs and are out of scope.

controls.name: Scopes
controls.what: Each client gets only the service.object.right scopes assigned.

controls.name: IP Whitelisting
controls.what: Rejects API requests from IPs or CIDRs not on the client's allowlist (403).

controls.name: Account Groups / Business Groups data access restrictions
controls.what: Limits a client-credentials client to transactional data in chosen account groups and master data in chosen business groups.
controls.setting: OAuth/OIDC Client Configuration > Account Groups / Business Groups

controls.name: Client Purpose
controls.what: Mandatory field recording whether the client is internal, third-party or marketplace.

controls.name: Revoke API Key
controls.what: Revokes the access and API permissions granted by the key.
controls.setting: Setup > Integrations > API Keys > edit key

controls.name: API key expiration date
controls.what: Optional date after which the key stops working (midnight UTC).

controls.name: API key Enable Permissions
controls.what: Restricts the key to selected APIs; unchecked allows all Coupa APIs.

controls_unknown: Whether deactivating a client invalidates already-issued 24h JWT access tokens.
Whether client secrets can be rotated without recreating the client, and whether they expire.
Admin audit log events for OAuth client creation, edits, secret views or deactivation.
Whether customers can view the API telemetry data (docs describe 'internal reporting').
Whether Coupa SAML SSO settings affect OAuth token use or API key use.
Whether any legacy API keys still authenticate on current releases.

credentials.name: OAuth2/OpenID Connect Client - Client Credentials grant

authentication.summary: An integrations-enabled admin creates an OAuth2/OIDC client with scopes. The integration posts client_id, client_secret and scopes to /oauth2/token and gets a 24-hour JWT access token.

federation.details: No user involved; docs do not discuss SSO or IdP conditional access for these tokens.

ip_restriction.boundary: Per-client IP Whitelisting; requests from other IPs get 403. Off unless configured.

lifetime.summary: Access token 24h; client secret has no documented expiry

renewal.summary: Integration requests a new token with the secret, recommended every 20 hours.

administration.summary: Setup > Integrations > Oauth2/OpenID Connect Clients: create, edit scopes, IP whitelisting, account/business group restrictions, Client Purpose, activate/deactivate.

offboard.details: Client credentials clients are used when no user is involved.

inventory.details: The OpenIDConnect Clients table at Setup > Integrations > Oauth2/OpenID Connect Clients lists clients.

expiry.api: Fixed 24h; read expires_in in the POST https://{instance}/oauth2/token response

log_sources.name: API telemetry
log_sources.notes: Collected automatically for OAuth client requests; AWS non-GovCloud/FedRAMP/HIPAA only; customer access not documented.

log_sources.name: Integration History Records / Integration Runs
log_sources.notes: Populated only if the integration writes them.

anomaly_cues: Client Purpose set to Third-Party for unknown providers
Clients without IP Whitelisting or group restrictions

containment.steps: Deactivate the client in Setup > Integrations > Oauth2/OpenID Connect Clients; add IP Whitelisting.

unknown: Which user/actor records show for client-credentials writes

calls.log_notes: API telemetry captures OAuth requests; customer visibility unclear.

credentials.name: OAuth2/OpenID Connect Client - Authorization Code / Device Code grant (user-delegated)

authentication.summary: A user signs in to Coupa and consents; the app gets an access token and, with offline_access, a refresh token acting as that user (e.g. Okta provisioning).

federation.details: The user authenticates to Coupa during consent (SSO if configured); later refresh-token use has no documented IdP check.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP Whitelisting is a field on OAuth/OIDC clients; docs do not limit it to client credentials. Account/business group restrictions apply only to client-credentials clients.

renewal.summary: App refreshes until the refresh token expires, then the user re-authenticates.

inventory.details: The OpenIDConnect Clients table lists clients, but docs name no view of which users authorized a client or their tokens.

inventory.ui: Setup > Integrations > Oauth2/OpenID Connect Clients (lists clients only, not per-user grants)

expiry.api: Fixed: refresh tokens expire every 90 days; not configurable in docs

token_format.notes: JWT access token; refresh token 90 days.

anomaly_cues: Authorization code clients requesting offline_access with write scopes
unknown: How to revoke one user's refresh token

authentication.summary: A 40-character key sent in the X-COUPA-API-KEY header. Tied to an API user equivalent to an admin. Deprecated; unsupported from R35.

federation.details: Static header key; docs do not address SSO.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP control documented for API keys.

lifetime.summary: Never expires unless an expiry date is set

renewal.summary: Same key reused; can be regenerated.

administration.summary: Setup > Integrations > API Keys: optional expiry, optional per-API permissions, revoke, regenerate.
administration.conditions: New keys no longer issued; existing keys should be revoked.

offboard.details: The key belongs to a dedicated API user, not a person's account.

inventory.details: Keys are managed and revoked under Setup > API Keys.

token_format.notes: 40-character case-sensitive alphanumeric key in X-COUPA-API-KEY header.

log_sources.name: Object Integration History
log_sources.notes: Key contact first/last name appears on the object's integration history when the key is used.

credential_id_fields.notes: Set when the key is created.

anomaly_cues: Any remaining active API key after OAuth migration
Keys with no expiry and no permissions set

containment.steps: Edit the key under Setup > Integrations > API Keys and use Revoke API Key.
containment.notes: Static key; revocation removes its API access.

calls.reveals: User records; key acts as admin-equivalent API user
calls.log_notes: Reads are not documented as logged; writes are attributed to the API user.
